tasks.title: Label lane v2: M3 vision for outlined-text firms + callout-vs-room filtering

prep.what: Productize the M3 vision-tiles lane so outlined-text firms get room labels — plus filter out non-room callouts (note paragraphs, stair arrows, FEC labels) that currently bleed into room names.
prep.understand: The free live-text lane reads zero words when a firm outlines all text (PDFTron style — the Harborview demo hit this live). The M3 tiles lane sends rasterized image tiles to a MiniMax vision LLM (~4.3 min/sheet, metered cost). Holabird proves the lane works (92/109 rooms named in prod). The secrets decision: MINIMAX_AI key must reach the VPS .env.
approach: Productize `docs/spike/run_labels_m3tiles.py` as an opt-in 'read labels (AI)' route on the service, gated behind the §7a metered-credits event.
Decide and wire MINIMAX_AI key to the VPS .env (secrets decision — key never in source).
Build callout-vs-room spatial filter: room labels sit INSIDE the room polygon, general notes and arrows are outside or have paragraph formatting.
Test on Harborview to confirm rooms go from 'unnamed' to labeled; check Holabird stays byte-identical on the live-text path.

prep.what: Build the full assembly-to-quantity engine: room classification → CSI assembly set → formulas → up to 8 quantities (floor tile area, wall paint SF, drywall SF, flooring LF, etc.). This is the last pillar before the Excel is estimator-grade.
prep.understand: `engine/assemblies.py` was scaffolded as 'assemblies-lite' in B1 but is not full. The full version needs a room-type → assembly lookup table keyed to CSI divisions. Wall height is the critical missing input — it converts perimeter to wall area for paint and drywall. The PATCH wall_height_ft route was already built during CT Pros Phase A (t28).
approach: Define the assembly lookup table in `engine/assemblies.py`: room_type → list of {quantity_key, formula, unit} — e.g. bathroom → {floor_tile: floor_sqft}, {wall_paint: perimeter × height}, {drywall: perimeter × height}.
Wire wall_height_ft: it already exists as a per-sheet PATCH parameter; make it available to the assembly calculator per-room (project default + optional per-room override).
For each room in the takeoff result, run assembly formulas and produce a named-quantity dict; add to the per-room JSON output.
Extend `engine/excel.py` to write quantity columns alongside the existing area/perimeter columns in the Excel sheets.
Run the gauntlet (should stay 85/85) and add 2-3 pytest cases validating known assembly outputs for a bathroom and an office.
resources: CSI division reference (Division 09 Finishes covers paint/flooring/tile)

tasks.title: Replace foreign-firm engine profiles with CT Pros blueprint CATEGORIES

prep.what: Confirm the engine-side GET /profiles endpoint on the VPS returns CT Pros blueprint categories in plain building language, and wire it so the Takeoff UI shows real labels — the app-side Vue code is already done (commit 4a8ef57).
prep.understand: App-side is DONE: Takeoff/Index.vue already fetches /takeoff-api/profiles, defaults to Auto (recommended), and static-falls-back on failure. What remains is ENGINE-side: the endpoint must return human-readable labels (School/institutional, High-rise CAD-flattened, Residential/multifamily…), exclude 'mitchell' (blind-eval holdout, never client-visible), and provide an Auto pseudo-profile that probes stroke widths on upload.
approach: SSH into azteam-vps, hit GET https://aztakeoff.azteamai.com/profiles and inspect the response — are labels human-readable or still the raw profile strings?
If raw strings: update `service/routes.py` to return a human-label registry dict instead of the raw profile list.
Add the 'auto' entry that probes stroke widths (the probe is already in `engine/probe.py` from CT Pros Phase A — just expose it at /profiles).
Ensure 'mitchell' is excluded from the list (it's the blind-eval holdout — annotate with a comment).
Test end-to-end: open the CT Pros app takeoff page and confirm the dropdown shows building categories, not profile code-names.

tasks.title: Derive wall PAINT area (perimeter x height) — the missing painting measurement

prep.what: Add wall paint square footage derivation to the takeoff seeder: wall_paint_sqft = perimeter × wall_height_ft per room. Right now a painting project seeded from takeoff gets ZERO wall area — the seeder drops geometry.
prep.understand: `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` currently discards room geometry (`meta.perimeter`). The perimeter IS in the engine's room JSON output (from `geometry.rings` or `meta.perimeter`). Wall height must come from a new `wall_height_ft` column on estimates (project-level default + optional per-room override). The painting labor rate already exists (t39 seeded it) so the line pricing should just work once quantities are right.
approach: Write a migration adding `wall_height_ft` (nullable decimal) to the `estimates` table; expose it as an editable field on the Estimate edit page (beside the estimate header, alongside floor_sqft).
In `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php`: stop dropping geometry — read `meta.perimeter` (or compute from `geometry.rings`) per room and pass it through.
Compute `wall_paint_sqft = perimeter × wall_height_ft` per room; emit as an EstimateLineItem with `kind='wall_paint'` using `LineItemFactory::fromMeasurement()`.
Wire the new `kind='wall_paint'` into the project-type-aware surface set so it only seeds on painting/remodel jobs (not flooring-only).
Add 2 PHPUnit tests: a room with known perimeter + height → expected wall_paint_sqft, and a zero-height guard (don't emit a $0 wall-paint line when height is unset).
resources: `LaborRateSeeder.php` (confirm painting labor rate rows from t39 exist)

tasks.title: Add PerLinearFt RateType (prerequisite for pricing trim/wall-linear)

prep.what: Add `per_linear_ft` to the RateType enum and seed a trim labor rate using it — a 30-minute prerequisite that unblocks pricing trim/wall-linear measurements (t48).
prep.understand: `app/Enums/RateType.php` currently has per-sqft, per-unit, and a few others but no per-linear-foot. `LineItemFactory::unitFromRateType()` maps each RateType to a unit label string (like 'sqft', 'unit'). Without PerLinearFt, trim measurements can't get a unit or a priced labor line.
approach: Add `PerLinearFt = 'per_linear_ft'` case to `app/Enums/RateType.php`; add its label in the `label()` method if the enum has one.
In `app/Services/LineItemFactory.php::unitFromRateType()`, add `'per_linear_ft' => 'lf'`.
In `database/seeders/LaborRateSeeder.php`, add a trim labor rate row: trade='trim', rate_type=per_linear_ft, rate=some_sensible_default.
Run `php artisan db:seed --class=LaborRateSeeder` in dev to verify no errors.
Check for any enum feature tests that enumerate RateType values and add PerLinearFt there.
resources: Test suite grep for RateType assertions
